subject: Re: Post-demo recap + quantization trade-offs / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice@finwave.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + quantization trade-offs / next steps

Hi Alice / Samir —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and recommended next steps from our side: 

1) Summary of what you asked for
- Low-latency customer support summaries (avg. 120 token responses)
- Tight cost targets (target < $0.003 / 1k tokens)
- On-prem option later this year for PII workloads

2) Our recommendation (initial model fit)
- Candidate models: Redwood-13B-OPT-ft (FP16) for baseline quality, Redwood-13B-AWQ (AWQ 4-bit) for throughput testing, and a GPTQ-quantized variant for lower memory footprint.
- Suggested eval sets: the prompt set I attached (finwave-prompt-set-v1.csv) and the short regression list we discussed.

3) Quantization trade-study plan (quick)
- Run AWQ 4-bit + GPTQ per-layer on your full prompt set, compare token-level perplexity, BLEU-ish metrics for structured outputs, and subjective quality via the 50-case review.
- FP8 (if you plan to run on recent HW) can help latency but needs careful calibration — we can include an FP8 run as an optional arm.

4) Next steps / asks from you
- Confirm which model outputs you care about (summaries only vs. structured entities).
- Share a small sample of 1k conversations (anonymized) for a fidelity run.
- Preferred time for a short quantization trade-study sync next week (30m).

I've attached a short trade-study PDF with the quick-run results from our sandbox and the prompt set. The spreadsheet includes token-level latency and quality comparisons across AWQ/GPTQ/FP16.

If this looks good I'll schedule a 30m readout with Rishi (inference lead) and Vivek (solutions) — we can walk through the trade-offs and pick the 2 arms to run against your full sample.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com

Attachments:
- finwave-quant-trade-study-AWQ-vs-GPTQ.pdf (summary, 6 pages)
- finwave-prompt-set-v1.csv (100 rows)
- quant-eval-results.xlsx (sandbox metrics)

From: Alice Johnson <alice@finwave.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@finwave.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + quantization trade-offs / next steps

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few quick clarifications from our side: 
- Output types: summaries + entity extraction (customer_name, issue_type, SLA_tier). We care about both free-text quality and structured reliability.
- We'll anonymize and drop PII, but can share ~800 conversations by Wednesday.
- FP8: our infra team is hesitant; they prefer well-supported quant stacks (GPTQ/AWQ). If FP8 shows large gains we can consider it but would want more validation.

Can you confirm the expected delta in latency / cost between AWQ and GPTQ for the Redwood-13B variants (ballpark)? Also, can you flag any regressions you saw in the sandbox when moving from FP16 -> AWQ 4-bit?

Happy to do the 30m sync next Thursday at 10am PT if that works for your team.

Best,
Alice
Head of ML Ops, FinWave

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice@finwave.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + quantization trade-offs / next steps

Hey Alice — great, Thursday 10am PT works for us. Quick answers before the sync so you can prep: 

Ballpark deltas (Redwood-13B):
- FP16 baseline (hosted runtime): median token latency 18ms, cost per 1k tokens: $0.012
- AWQ 4-bit: median token latency ~10–12ms (15–40% improvement), cost per 1k tokens: ~ $0.0048 (depends on batching)
- GPTQ (per-layer) quant: latency ~11–14ms, cost per 1k tokens: ~ $0.0055
- FP8 (experimental path): can hit 8–10ms token latency but we saw occasional instability on corner-case numerical ops; requires extra calibration and validation.

Quality / regression notes from our sandbox (FP16 -> AWQ 4-bit):
- Most prompts (85%) show negligible quality delta on summary tasks.
- Structured extraction (entity labels) saw small precision drops (~2–4%) on edge cases where tokenization shifted; we include a calibration step to tune tokenization and token merging heuristics.
- We observed a small number of hallucination regressions in very long-context prompts (~1% of cases) — we flagged these in the attached spreadsheet with examples.

Attachments in our Drive folder include prompt-by-prompt deltas so you can scan which examples regressed. We'll prioritize entity extraction cases for the full run.

For the Thursday sync I propose this agenda: 1) confirm eval dataset + success metrics; 2) pick 2 quant arms (AWQ 4-bit, GPTQ) + optional FP8; 3) timeline and deliverables (2-week sandbox run).

I'll send a calendar invite. Thanks!
Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 08:40:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo recap + quantization trade-offs / next steps

Marissa / Vivek —

Looping in a few internal notes ahead of the call:
- I reviewed the sandbox spreadsheet. Early take: AWQ gives best perf/cost for 13B with modest quality impact after calibration — matches our slides.
- GPTQ is simpler to integrate on customer infra that already runs GPTQ toolchain, but slightly worse latency in our tests and larger disk footprint for some configs.
- FP8: keep as optional. If FinWave insists we can run a limited validation but call it "experimental" in the proposal.

Action items before the readout:
- Marissa: confirm the subset of 50 priority prompts that we will hand off for manual review (Alice said entity edge cases are priority).
- Vivek: prepare short notes on migration path for on-prem + KMS considerations.
- I'll get the draft quant-side SOW language to attach to the proposal.

Rishi
VP, Inference
